title: Hiding Self-Application Inside rec
description: Wrap self(self)(n) in a helper parameter rec so the factorial body looks like an ordinary recursive function.

steps.description: In step2, pass lambda n: self(self)(n) as the argument rec into lambda rec: lambda n: 1 if n == 0 else n * rec(n - 1).
The factorial logic on line 3 calls rec(n - 1), while line 4 supplies the self-application wrapper lambda n: self(self)(n).

steps.question: Why is rec defined as lambda n: self(self)(n) instead of just self(self)?
steps.answer: Wrapping self(self) inside lambda n delays calling self(self) until rec is actually invoked on n - 1, preventing infinite recursion in an eager language like Python.

steps.description: Construct factorial_v2 = step2(step2) and evaluate factorial_v2(6) to print 720.
Trace factorial_v2(6) to see rec(n - 1) invoke lambda n: self(self)(n) on each recursive step.
